intro: Every match has a start. In a judo room, players bow. In a wrestling room, they shake hands. In a boxing ring, a bell rings. In a school gym, a whistle blows.
Each signal has a history. It comes from a place and a people. Old paintings, books and records help us learn these stories.
In this unit, you will name the signals different rooms use. You will learn where they come from. You will tell a legend apart from a record.
bigQuestion: How do people start a match fairly, and how do we learn where those ways came from?

Greek writers say boxing joins the ancient Olympics
The Nihon Shoki, with a sumo legend, is finished in Japan
The Queensberry Rules set three-minute boxing rounds
Kano Jigoro starts the Kodokan judo school in Tokyo
Joseph Hudson makes the Acme Thunderer whistle in England
Fencing is part of the first modern Olympics
Judo joins the Olympics in Tokyo
Women's judo joins the Olympics in Barcelona
Taekwondo joins the Olympics in Sydney

test.q: What do many judo players do when they step onto the mat?
test.why: In many judo schools, students bow when they step onto the mat.

test.q: Where does the sumo salt custom come from?
choices: Shinto, an old religion of Japan
test.why: The salt custom comes from Shinto.

test.q: Which sport has a salute in its rule book?
test.why: The world fencing rule book asks fencers to salute.
Wrestlers shake hands before and after a match.

test.q: What rings to start a boxing round?
test.why: The timekeeper rings a bell to start each round.

test.q: Who made the Acme Thunderer whistle in 1884?
test.why: Joseph Hudson made the whistle in Birmingham, England.

test.q: What country do the Beni Hasan wrestler paintings come from?
test.why: Beni Hasan is in Egypt, near the Nile River.

test.q: Why can we read Kano Jigoro's ideas today?
test.why: Kano wrote talks and articles about judo.

test.q: What year did judo join the Olympics?
test.why: Judo joined the Olympics in Tokyo in 1964.

test.q: What is the difference between a legend and a record?
choices: a record is written down as it happened; a legend cannot be proved
test.why: Historians keep legends, which cannot be proved, apart from records.

write.prompt: Pick two ways a match can start from this unit, like the judo bow and the boxing bell. Tell which sport uses each one. Tell where it comes from. Use one real date, like 1882 or 1867.
